identity.title: Diffuse X-Ray-emitting Gas in the Central Region of Star-forming Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use archival data from $Chandra$ observations to extract the diffuse X-ray emission from 23 nearby star-forming galaxies and study its correlation with star formation activity in the central region of these galaxies.
The CO(2-1) data for our sample galaxies were obtained from the PHANGS-ALMA Large Program

The PHANGS survey selects galaxies with distances less than 24 Mpc

question.value: How does diffuse thermal X-ray luminosity of hot gas in the central regions of 23 nearby star-forming galaxies scale with SFR, spatial scale, stellar mass, molecular gas and baryonic mass?

evidence.quote: we aim to investigate the scaling relation of $L_{\rm 0.5 - 2\,keV}^{\rm gas}$ with SFR on different spatial scales and examine its scale dependence in the central region of the 23 sample galaxies.
The CO(2-1) data for our sample galaxies were obtained from the PHANGS-ALMA Large Program
These data include both interferometric and single-dish observations

findings_qualitative.value: Central L_X-SFR slope is super-linear and decreases with aperture radius, reaching the global level by ~2.5 kpc

evidence.quote: Its slope anticorrelates with spatial scale up to 2.5 kpc, where it drops to the global level.

claims.hypothesis: Central diffuse X-ray luminosity scales super-linearly with SFR
claims.experiment: Chandra diffuse X-ray luminosity vs WISE/GALEX SFR for 23 galaxies, LINMIX_ERR fit
claims.result: slope 1.34±0.16 for center vs 0.93 disk, 1.08 global
claims.finding: Stronger star formation gives more efficient X-ray conversion in centers

evidence.quote: we found a super-linear relation of ${\rm log}(L_{\rm 0.5-2\,keV}^{\rm gas} /{\rm erg\,s^{-1}})=1.34\,{\rm log}({\rm SFR}/{M_{\rm \odot}}\,{\rm yr^{-1}})+40.15$

claims.hypothesis: SFR is a better predictor of hot gas emission than M_star, M_mol, M_b
claims.result: M_mol and M_b scatter 0.58, M_star 0.68, vs SFR 0.41

evidence.quote: We conclude that the star formation rate is a better predictor for diffuse X-ray emission than stellar mass, molecular gas, and baryonic mass.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two-component APEC+power-law model rejected as it did not improve fits

evidence.quote: we found that the two-component spectral model does not significantly improve the fitting results or better constrain the parameters.

limitations_admitted.value: Unresolved faint sources cannot be excluded

evidence.quote: Although this cannot currently be excluded, we estimate the contribution of faint compact sources to be less than 30%
